lots.what_it_is: Oak longcase (grandfather) clock in 1920s-30s English style: arched silvered and engraved dial with Roman chapter ring and a 'Tempus Fugit' motto boss in the arch, blind-fret trunk door with glazed window, chrome spherical pendulum bob, ogee bracket feet. No maker name seen. No winding holes on the dial and a chain visible in the trunk, so likely a chain-wound movement (age and maker unknown; could be 1930s British or a later reproduction).

lots.guide_summary: Same-item or close entries run A$210-400: three SOLD (Gowans Tempus Fugit A$210 in 2026; Danielle Elizabeth A$320 in 2023; Eastbourne GBP130 = about A$260 in 2021 at 2.0 AUD/GBP assumed) and one UNSOLD (Theodore Bruce passed at estimate A$200-400, 2024). No ASKING entries. Wider Tasmanian category sales of longcase clocks at Gowans in the last 13 months run A$70-360 hammer, median about A$200. Nothing is an exact match.
lots.working: Keep: lowest in-window close SOLD = Gowans Tempus Fugit A$210 hammer (Feb 2026). 210 / 1.22 = 172.1, round down to A$170 hammer (A$207 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$200 hammer at a Tasmanian room (Gowans category median about A$200, close Tempus Fugit A$210). Less about 15% seller commission and fees = A$170 net, no postage (bulky, local pickup sale). 170 / 2.44 = 69.7, round down to A$65. Flip margin is very thin; this is a keep-only lot. Inbound freight A$0 but a longcase needs a trailer or van and two people from 9 Goodman Crt.
lots.confidence_reason: Only a motto (Tempus Fugit) is readable, no maker; movement not seen; only one in-window close SOLD (and that a newer German reproduction); the rest are category guides or older than 24 months.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans lot 416690 Liddall & Sons A$1,400 (named maker, different class, not comparable). Lawsons 2019 Oak Cased Grandfather Clock passed at est A$800-1,200: page opened and data confirmed, but 2019 and no description, so dropped as not comparable. Gowans lot 432076 Enfield moved from close to category guide after viewing its photo. Researcher's 'tubular chimes' claim not supported by the photos (one chain and a spherical bob visible, no tubes).
lots.key_photo_findings: Dial arch boss reads 'Tempus Fugit' in script (motto, not a maker). Silvered engraved dial with Roman chapter ring and minute track, blued or blackened pierced hands. No winding holes on the dial, a single chain and chrome spherical pendulum bob visible in the trunk window, suggesting a chain-wound movement. Oak case with blind fret door panel, fielded base panel, ogee bracket feet. Light tarnish streaking on the dial. Tag 'S67/2' on the dial.
lots.condition: Case looks sound with even colour and no obvious breaks; dial lightly tarnished; movement, weights, chimes and running order not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is it going and does it strike or chime? Is the movement chain-wound or key-wound, and is there any maker's name or stamp on the movement or backplate? Are all weights, the pendulum and the key present, and is the trunk glass intact?

lots.what_it_is: Watercolour of a mountain across a bay with granite foreshore and heath (Tasmanian east coast style), signed lower right, partly legible as '...ff T..son', consistent with Geoff (Geoffrey) Tyson, 1911-1986, Launceston watercolourist and teacher held by QVMAG, TMAG and AWM. Window mount, pale timber frame. The neighbouring lot 1015 (cdid 3089306) is another Tyson watercolour with a biography note, which supports the attribution.
lots.guide_summary: No verified prices. Leads only: AASD (snippet only) says 15 Tyson works offered since 1989, 13 sold; Artrecord lists about 12 works on paper at Gowans, Colville and Leonard Joel, prices paywalled and the page returned 429 to me. Gowans API (tyson, geoffrey tyson, g tyson, cataract gorge, cradle mountain dove lake) found no Tyson artworks, apparently covering only recent sales.
